variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Apply the memory update before choosing the subgoal. Each episode starts with A: with the hand empty and remaining_targets nonempty, pick up the container identified by its first location. Point inside that container in the current image, using its visible center or another interior grasp point; small centroid shifts do not change identity. After execution shows a successful grasp and lift, the hand is holding a container. If remaining_targets is still nonempty, choose B to put down the held container before attempting the next target. After the release sequence leaves the hand open and empty, choose A at the first remaining target. A completed last requested pickup finishes the task; do not deliberately put that last container down as part of the goal. Do not infer an empty hand solely from stationary container detections: use the closing, lifting, and release observations. For an unexpected additional decision or an otherwise unmatched situation, choose B if the hand appears to hold a container; otherwise choose A at the closest visible container to the first remaining location. If that list is empty or no target can be located, choose B as the conservative menu fallback rather than inventing a new target.

fields.name: remaining_targets
fields.description: With empty incoming memory, use the demonstration to associate each requested cube with the container placed over it, then track that container through all subsequent movement. Track each moving container over the entire interval from departure to settling. Use continuity and direction of travel across the intermediate demonstration frames to assign its settled endpoint, resolving a moving pair jointly with the other container's complementary path. Do not reset an identity to the nearest original position or preserve detection-list order. Returning to the same unordered set of occupied positions is not evidence that identities have returned and is not a second exchange. One observed exchange switches the tracked containers' position assignments; only a further observed exchange of those identities restores the original assignment. Compute these intermediate tracks from the demonstration currently shown; persist only the resulting ordered list of final target locations. Write the final container centers as an ordered list of [y, x] locations in goal order, including the target being selected now. In these observations the initial lists are: episode 14 [[106, 150]]; episode 28 [[84, 90], [92, 133]]; episode 53 [[80, 117], [121, 102]]; episode 80 [[105, 122], [73, 128]]; episode 90 [[124, 101]]. With existing memory, remove the first entry only when the execution frames shown at this decision show the hand descending to that target, closing around a container, and lifting with fingers still partly open around it. The observed successful grasps finish near 46% opening at raised height; unchanged reported container centers do not negate that grasp evidence. A release sequence, with descent followed by opening and withdrawal, leaves the list unchanged. Otherwise preserve the incoming list. Never remove an entry in anticipation of the command chosen now. e.g. [[121, 102]]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of [y, x] container locations for requested pickups not yet completed. At the first decision, identify the container initially covering each requested cube, follow its identity through the entire demonstration, and list its final location in the order specified by the goal. Follow each container's full directed path through intermediate demonstration frames, from departure to its settled endpoint, rather than using original cube locations or the sorted order of detections. When a pair moves, assign endpoints using those individual paths. A return to the same unordered set of occupied positions does not establish that identities have returned and must not be counted as an additional exchange. One observed exchange of the tracked containers switches their position assignments; only a further observed exchange restores them. Ignore extra containers unless they cover a requested cube. Initialization for these episodes is: episode 14 [[106, 150]]; episode 28 [[84, 90], [92, 133]]; episode 53 [[80, 117], [121, 102]]; episode 80 [[105, 122], [73, 128]]; episode 90 [[124, 101]]. At the decision immediately following a successful requested pickup, remove the first entry. Do not remove an entry merely because a pickup is selected at the current decision. Putting a container down leaves the list unchanged. Thus, at steps 2 and 3 of each two-target episode, the list contains only the second target. Locations identify containers rather than requiring exact pixel agreement. e.g. [[121, 102]]

history.critique:
field remaining_targets, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  When the goal requested the red-covering container, two containers moved around one another and finished at the same unordered pair of occupied positions. The policy selected the red container's original position, [111, 111], and wrote [[111, 111]], whereas the demonstration identity assignment requires [[99, 155]]. This exposes a PREDICTABILITY failure in interpreting exchanges, leading to the wrong target. Clarify that returning to the same set of occupied positions does not mean identities have returned: count exchanges by the paths of the individual containers, not by recurrence of the unordered position set. Across each movement interval, follow the full directed paths through intermediate frames to the settled endpoints. In the relevant pattern, the red identity follows [111, 111], [99, 117], [91, 137], then the endpoint near [99, 155]; this is one exchange, not two. Keep remaining_targets as the ordered list of final container locations for requested pickups not yet completed. Initialize it after tracking the entire demonstration, for example [[99, 155]], and remove its first entry only at the decision showing the completed requested pickup. Release leaves it unchanged. No additional memory field is needed.

field remaining_targets, POLICY PROMPT
  When asked to pick up the red-covering container after a demonstration in which a moving pair ended at the same unordered positions it initially occupied, the policy chose the original red position and wrote [[111, 111]] instead of the required [[99, 155]]. The generic continuity and exchange instructions left the sparse-frame identity association unresolved, breaking PREDICTABILITY and consequently target selection. Clarify initialization using the demonstration visible at the first decision: associate cubes with their covers, then track each moving pair over the entire interval from departure to settling. Use the direction of travel across intermediate frames to resolve the endpoint assignment; do not reset identity to the nearest original position, or count a return of the unordered position set as a second exchange. For example, a cover starting at [111, 111] and moving through [99, 117] and [91, 137] continues toward the endpoint near [99, 155], while the other cover takes the complementary path. Only a further observed exchange of those tracked identities restores their original assignment. Write the resulting ordered list of requested final locations, such as [[99, 155]], including the pickup selected now. Retain the existing observable update rule: remove the head when the current execution frames show the successful descent, closure around the target, and lift; do not remove it when merely selecting a pickup, and preserve the list through release. The list remains the only persistent field; intermediate tracks are computed from the currently shown demonstration.
